page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with Hebrew words set inline in the text. Below the last line, at the right, the catchword "Re-".

main_text.p: 1. Musicam seu cantus rationem apud Judæos designare, qui textum Biblicum cantillant.
2. Pronunciationem legitimam, in syllabæ elevatione designare.
Usus primus Judæis relinquitur: secundus habet has regulas..
1. Omnis dictio habet accentum tonicum, nisi habeat post se virgulam quæ Maccaph dicitur, [−]

2. Syllaba quæ habet accentum tonicum acuitur, exceptis Telisha majori, Jethis, Paschta & Telischa minori, Sægolta, & Sarka, quæ primæ vel ultimæ vocis literæ semper adhærent, sed eam non semper afficiunt.
3. Ejusdem accentus in eadem voce geminati, prior syllabam acuit, diversorum posterior, ut תֹהוּ tóhu. וְהָאֵצִים [?] vehaetzím.
4. Accentus tonicus vocali longæ additus, Scheva sequens constituit quiescens, ut תַּגְלֶנָה [?] tagélna.
Tertius usus orationis membra spectat, & sic distinguuntur in Ministros & Reges.
Ministri sunt 8. Munach, Mahpach, Merca simplex, & duplex, Darga, Jerach, Kadma, Telischa Ketanna, qui cùm nihil distinguant, ideo nullius fere usus sunt nec in aliis linguis usurpantur.

page.notes: The Hebrew word after "tóhu." is only partly legible; the vowel points and letters are doubtful, hence [?]. The Hebrew for "tagélna" is also uncertain. The Maccaph example "[−]" is printed as shown. The "8." before Munach appears as a plain numeral in the scan. Printing errors left as printed: "cùm", "Sægolta" spelling, "secundus" spelling as printed in the scan. Long s was read as plain s throughout, so "f" forms like "fimplex" and "Miniftri" are rendered with s.
